zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 1; they obstruct downward and outward views from Ocean View cabins on Decks 1, 2, and to a lesser extent Deck 6.
zones.effect: Ocean View cabins on Deck 1 look directly into or over the boats; Deck 2 looks down at them; Deck 6 forward and aft may catch the top edge depending on exact position.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to anyone wanting open ocean views or natural light; irrelevant to Interior cabin guests or those prioritizing price over vista.

zones.what: Lido Deck pool area, buffet, and outdoor activities are directly above Deck 9 midship and aft sections.
zones.effect: Daytime foot traffic, deck chair dragging, pool sounds, and music carry through; activity runs from early breakfast until late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone sensitive to overhead noise should avoid; doesn't bother those out enjoying the ship most of the day.

zones.what: Deck 9 aft contains public venues and outdoor spaces directly above Deck 8 aft cabins.
zones.effect: Overhead noise and vibration from foot traffic and venue activity, though less intense than directly under the Lido pool area.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to noise-sensitive guests; one deck of separation helps but doesn't eliminate sound transmission.

zones.what: Main dining rooms, galley operations, and public venues are on Decks 2 and 3, directly below Deck 6 forward and midship cabins.
zones.effect: Kitchen noise, plate clattering, and ventilation hum carry upward, especially during meal service times (breakfast, lunch, dinner rushes).
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those wanting quiet evenings and early mornings; background noise is persistent but not usually intrusive.

zones.what: Main theatre (Toulouse-Lautrec) is located on Decks 3-4, two to three decks below Deck 6 forward cabins.
zones.effect: Show music and sound effects can carry upward during performances (typically early and late evening); distance attenuates but doesn't eliminate bass tones.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers or early-to-bed guests may notice; most find it minor given the vertical distance.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks are located forward and midship on all cabin decks, with stair towers adjacent.
zones.effect: Cabins near elevator/stair banks benefit from quick vertical access but experience intermittent hallway traffic, door chimes, and conversation noise at all hours.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests benefit from proximity; light sleepers should request cabins away from banks; severity varies by how close the cabin is.

zones.what: Engine room and propulsion machinery are located low and aft; vibration and low-frequency hum are most noticeable in aft cabins on the lowest guest decks.
zones.effect: A persistent low rumble and subtle vibration underfoot, most noticeable when engines are working (maneuvering, sea days at speed); white noise effect for some, annoying for others.
zones.mattersTo: Sensitive sleepers or those bothered by vibration should avoid; many guests don't notice or find it soothing; worsens in rough seas.

zones.what: Bow thrusters are located forward below the waterline; they create vibration and mechanical noise during docking and maneuvering in port.
zones.effect: Brief but noticeable vibration and rumbling during arrivals and departures; can wake early sleepers on port mornings.
zones.mattersTo: Matters only during maneuvering (15-30 minutes per port); deep sleepers won't notice, light sleepers should be aware.

zones.what: Anchor chain runs through the bow; deployment and retrieval create loud mechanical noise and vibration in forward cabins on lower decks.
zones.effect: Sharp metallic rumbling every time the ship anchors or weighs anchor, typically early morning in tender ports; brief but unmistakable.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers in tender-heavy itineraries should avoid bow cabins; doesn't affect ships docking pier-side.

unknowns: Whether this Conquest-class hull has a pronounced hump (cantilevered balconies on lower-mid decks) and if so, the exact deck range; this feature is common on contemporary ships but I cannot confirm specifics for this class without cross-referencing deck plans.
The exact location and extent of the I-95 crew corridor access points and which cabin sections experience the most service traffic.
Specific connecting cabin pairs or ADA-accessible cabin distribution beyond what's visible in aggregate counts.
Whether recent refurbishments have altered soundproofing or repositioned any public venues that would change noise profiles.
